doc.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: What makes him angry and his weekly prayer
summary: Disrespect makes him angry; he describes his Monday ritual and philosophy.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: All three of you gentlemen seem at ease with others and fairly peaceful. And I’m wondering what makes you angry?
It could be a musical thing or perhaps —

For me, disrespect. When somebody talks to me in a certain way and there’s no reason for it, that makes me angry. You know like you’re very respectful you know. Students can be disrespectful. They don’t make me angry but they get annoying, it’s like don’t do that. When you talk to me at least talk to me — you can disagree with me but don’t disrespect me. That’s my philosophy with life pretty much. Just treat others the way you expect to be treated, and if they do it most of the time I’ll call them out on it, just don’t talk to me that way, don’t treat me that way and I’ll do the same. That’s like my prayer for the week. On Mondays I do a certain thing, a little ritual, and I always say, I ask the higher beings, including God, help me — I ask for guidance and I always say, “Help me, guide me in saying the right things and doing the right things so that I can not only help myself and improve myself but help others in the process.” And that’s what I live by on a weekly basis. I do that prayer at least — on Mondays before I go anywhere.
I think your students are probably lucky that they have you.
